_description: OBD-II Diagnostic Trouble Codes — common P-codes with causes, tests, and advisor summaries for the Repair Assistant module

P0011.name: A Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
tests: check timing chain stretch with scope
listen for timing chain rattle on cold start
P0011.advisor_summary: The computer detected that your engine's camshaft timing is off — it's more advanced than it should be. This is often caused by low or dirty oil. We need to diagnose the root cause before it worsens.

P0016.name: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation Bank 1 Sensor A
tests: verify timing chain condition via scope
P0016.advisor_summary: Your engine's timing chain or sensors are out of sync. This can indicate the timing chain is stretched and may be close to failing. We recommend not driving until this is diagnosed.

P0030.name: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0030.advisor_summary: One of your oxygen sensors has a heater circuit issue. Oxygen sensors help your engine manage fuel efficiently — we can diagnose and replace if needed.

P0068.name: MAP/MAF — Throttle Position Correlation
tests: compare MAF and MAP readings at idle
P0068.advisor_summary: Your engine's air pressure and throttle sensors are giving conflicting readings. This usually points to an air leak or a failing sensor, and can affect how smoothly your engine runs.

P0100.name: Mass Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
tests: inspect and clean MAF sensor with MAF cleaner
P0100.advisor_summary: The sensor that measures how much air enters your engine is malfunctioning. A dirty or failing air flow sensor causes poor fuel economy and rough running.

P0101.name: Mass Air Flow Sensor Range/Performance
tests: monitor MAF grams/sec at idle and WOT
P0101.advisor_summary: Your mass air flow sensor is reading outside its normal range. Often this just needs cleaning, but sometimes requires replacement. Affects fuel efficiency and engine response.

P0102.name: Mass Air Flow Sensor Circuit Low Input
tests: inspect wiring for short to ground
P0102.advisor_summary: The mass air flow sensor is sending a low signal to the computer. This can cause rough idle and starting issues.

P0113.name: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
tests: check IAT sensor resistance vs. temperature chart
P0113.advisor_summary: The sensor that measures incoming air temperature is reading too high. This is a minor issue that can affect fuel trim — usually a simple sensor or wiring fix.

P0128.name: Coolant Temperature Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature
tests: monitor coolant temp with scan tool during warm-up
verify thermostat opens at correct temp
P0128.advisor_summary: Your engine isn't reaching normal operating temperature — usually caused by a thermostat stuck in the open position. A failed thermostat is inexpensive and easy to replace, and fixing it improves heater performance and fuel economy.

P0171.name: System Too Lean Bank 1
tests: monitor short and long-term fuel trims
P0171.advisor_summary: Your engine is running lean — it's getting too much air or not enough fuel. Common causes are a small air leak or a dirty air flow sensor. We'll pinpoint the source and fix it.

P0172.name: System Too Rich Bank 1
causes: faulty coolant temp sensor causing over-fueling
P0172.advisor_summary: Your engine is running rich — too much fuel is being burned. This causes poor fuel economy and can damage the catalytic converter over time.

P0174.name: System Too Lean Bank 2
causes: vacuum leak (intake manifold, PCV, brake booster)
P0174.advisor_summary: The right bank of your engine is running lean (too much air, not enough fuel). Common cause is a small vacuum leak or dirty air flow sensor.

P0175.name: System Too Rich Bank 2
P0175.advisor_summary: The right side of your engine is running with too much fuel. Left uncorrected, this wastes fuel and can damage the catalytic converter.

P0190.name: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
tests: compare actual fuel pressure to sensor reading
P0190.advisor_summary: The sensor monitoring your fuel system pressure has a circuit issue. This affects how well your engine manages fuel delivery and can cause starting or running problems.

P0201.name: Injector Circuit Malfunction — Cylinder 1
tests: test injector pulse with noid light
P0201.advisor_summary: Cylinder 1's fuel injector circuit has a fault. The injector may be failed or there's a wiring issue. This causes a misfire on that cylinder.

P0263.name: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance Fault
tests: cylinder contribution test with scan tool
P0263.advisor_summary: Cylinder 1 isn't contributing its fair share of power. This is often a dirty or failing fuel injector. We'll test the injector and cylinder health.

P0300.name: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
tests: check spark plugs condition and gap
P0300.advisor_summary: Multiple cylinders are misfiring — your engine is not firing consistently in one or more cylinders. This causes the rough running/shaking you may feel. Often it's worn spark plugs, but we'll pinpoint the exact cause.

P0301.name: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
tests: swap spark plug and coil from cyl 1 to another cylinder — if misfire follows, that component is bad
P0301.advisor_summary: Cylinder 1 is misfiring — it's not firing as it should. This is usually a worn spark plug or a failed ignition coil, both of which are straightforward repairs.

P0302.name: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
tests: swap cyl 2 spark plug and coil
P0302.advisor_summary: Cylinder 2 is misfiring. Usually a spark plug or ignition coil — a quick swap test will confirm the cause.

P0303.name: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
tests: swap spark plug and coil from cyl 3
P0303.advisor_summary: Cylinder 3 is misfiring. We'll identify whether it's a plug, coil, injector, or compression issue.

P0304.name: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
tests: swap plug and coil from cyl 4
P0304.advisor_summary: Cylinder 4 is misfiring. Common causes are a worn spark plug or a failed ignition coil — both quick fixes when caught early.

P0316.name: Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
symptoms: shaking on startup that clears up
tests: check spark plugs for oil fouling
monitor fuel trims at cold start
P0316.advisor_summary: Your engine misfires briefly when first started. This often points to worn spark plugs or an issue with how the engine starts up from cold.

P0340.name: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction Bank 1
tests: check CMP sensor signal with scope
P0340.advisor_summary: The sensor that tracks your camshaft position has a circuit fault. This sensor is critical for starting and running — a failed one can cause a no-start condition.

P0351.name: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
causes: faulty spark plug causing coil failure
tests: swap ignition coil to another cylinder and see if misfire follows
P0351.advisor_summary: The ignition coil for cylinder 1 has a fault. Ignition coils create the spark to fire each cylinder — a failed coil causes a misfire. Often replaced along with the spark plug.

P0401.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
tests: command EGR open with scan tool and observe idle change
visually inspect EGR valve for carbon buildup
P0401.advisor_summary: Your exhaust gas recirculation system isn't flowing enough. The EGR valve is often clogged with carbon buildup over time. A cleaning or replacement usually resolves this.

P0402.name: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
tests: command EGR closed and check if idle smooths out
P0402.advisor_summary: Your EGR valve is stuck open or flowing too much exhaust gas. This typically causes rough idle and stalling — the valve usually needs cleaning or replacement.

P0410.name: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction
tests: inspect air injection ports for blockage
P0410.advisor_summary: Your secondary air injection system (which helps cold-start emissions) has a fault. This doesn't typically affect drivability but will cause a failed emissions test.

P0420.name: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
causes: oil burning into exhaust contaminating catalyst
O2 sensor fault giving false reading
tests: monitor upstream vs downstream O2 sensor switching with scan tool
check for misfires or oil/coolant consumption first
P0420.advisor_summary: Your catalytic converter is not cleaning exhaust gases efficiently enough. A catalytic converter lasts 100,000+ miles normally — if it's failing, we need to check whether a misfire or oil issue has been feeding it harmful exhaust that shortened its life.

P0430.name: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
tests: monitor downstream O2 bank 2 switching behavior
P0430.advisor_summary: The catalytic converter on the right bank of your engine is below efficiency spec. We'll determine whether the converter needs replacement and address any root causes.

P0440.name: Evaporative Emission Control System Malfunction
tests: check gas cap seal and tighten/replace
command purge solenoid open with scan tool
P0440.advisor_summary: Your vehicle's evaporative emission system has a fault — this system captures fuel vapors from the gas tank. The most common and easiest fix is a loose or faulty gas cap. We'll check that first before more complex diagnosis.

P0441.name: Evaporative Emission Control System Incorrect Purge Flow
tests: check purge line for kinks or cracks
monitor purge flow during active test
P0441.advisor_summary: The purge solenoid in your EVAP system is not flowing correctly. It's a component that manages fuel vapors from the gas tank. Usually a solenoid replacement resolves this.

P0442.name: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
tests: check and replace gas cap first
smoke test EVAP system to locate leak
P0442.advisor_summary: There's a small leak in your fuel vapor system — the most common cause is a loose or damaged gas cap. We'll start there before doing more involved diagnosis.

P0455.name: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.advisor_summary: There's a significant leak in your fuel vapor system. Check that your gas cap is fully tightened first — if that's not it, we'll use a smoke test to find the larger leak quickly.

P0456.name: Evaporative Emission Control System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
tests: replace gas cap and clear code first
P0456.advisor_summary: There's a very small leak in your fuel vapor system. The first step is replacing the gas cap, which fixes this issue about 30% of the time at minimal cost.

P0480.name: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit Malfunction
P0480.advisor_summary: Your electric cooling fan has a control circuit fault. The cooling fan is critical — without it, your car can overheat in stop-and-go traffic. This needs prompt attention.

P0500.name: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
tests: monitor VSS signal with scan tool while driving
P0500.advisor_summary: Your vehicle speed sensor has a fault. This sensor tells the transmission and computer how fast you're going. A failing VSS can cause erratic shifting and a non-functional speedometer.

P0505.name: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
tests: clean throttle body and IAC valve
test IAC with scan tool (command open/close)
P0505.advisor_summary: Your idle control system isn't functioning properly. The idle air control valve manages how much air enters the engine at idle — when it's dirty or stuck, you get rough or erratic idle. Often a thorough cleaning is all it needs.

P0507.name: Idle Air Control System RPM High
tests: check IAC position with scan tool
P0507.advisor_summary: Your engine idle is running too high. The most common cause is a vacuum leak letting extra air in, which tricks the engine into running faster. We'll find the leak and fix it.

P0562.name: System Voltage Low
tests: inspect battery terminals and ground straps
P0562.advisor_summary: Your vehicle's charging system voltage is too low. This usually points to a failing alternator or a battery that can no longer hold a charge. Left unchecked, you risk being stranded with a dead vehicle.

P0606.name: PCM/ECM Processor Fault
causes: poor PCM ground or power supply
tests: verify PCM power and grounds first
check for software update/reflash before condemning
test with known-good PCM if available
P0606.advisor_summary: Your vehicle's main computer may have an internal fault. Before replacing the PCM (which is expensive), we'll verify power and grounds and check for available software updates.

P0700.name: Transmission Control System Malfunction
tests: check transmission fluid level and condition
monitor trans data with scan tool during drive cycle
P0700.advisor_summary: Your transmission control system has flagged a fault. This triggers alongside a more specific transmission code — we'll pull the full set of codes to find the exact cause before recommending repair.

P0715.name: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
tests: check sensor signal with scan tool during driving
inspect sensor tip for metal debris
P0715.advisor_summary: Your transmission's input speed sensor has a fault. This sensor helps the transmission make smooth, accurate shift decisions. A failed sensor can cause harsh or erratic shifting.

P0720.name: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
tests: monitor OSS signal with scan tool while driving
P0720.advisor_summary: Your transmission's output speed sensor has a circuit fault. This can cause erratic speedometer readings and poor shift quality.

P0730.name: Incorrect Gear Ratio
tests: check transmission fluid level and condition
P0730.advisor_summary: Your transmission is not achieving the correct gear ratio — it's slipping or engaging the wrong gear. This needs to be diagnosed promptly to avoid further internal damage.

P0741.name: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
tests: monitor TCC operation with scan tool
check transmission fluid condition for burnt smell or debris
P0741.advisor_summary: Your torque converter clutch isn't locking up properly on the highway. This hurts fuel economy significantly and can eventually damage the transmission. The solenoid may need replacing, or in worse cases, the converter itself.

P0750.name: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction
tests: command solenoid on/off with scan tool
P0750.advisor_summary: A shift solenoid in your transmission has failed. Shift solenoids control how and when your transmission changes gears. A fluid service sometimes resolves this — otherwise solenoid replacement is needed.

P0840.name: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
tests: compare measured line pressure to spec
P0840.advisor_summary: Your transmission's fluid pressure sensor has a fault. We'll check the fluid level first — if it's low, that's the likely cause. Otherwise, the sensor may need replacement.

P1000.name: OBD Systems Readiness Test Not Complete
tests: complete OBD drive cycle per manufacturer procedure
verify all readiness monitors set to 'ready'
P1000.advisor_summary: Your vehicle's on-board diagnostic monitors haven't completed their self-tests yet. This happens after a battery disconnect or after codes are cleared. You'll need to drive the vehicle through a specific cycle to set all monitors before an emissions test.

P1101.name: Mass Air Flow Out of Self-Test Range (Ford)
tests: compare MAF reading to spec at idle
P1101.advisor_summary: Your Ford's air flow sensor is reading outside the expected range during self-test. Cleaning the MAF sensor often resolves this.

P1130.name: Lack of HO2S Switch Sensor Indicates Lean (Toyota/Lexus)
P1130.advisor_summary: Your Toyota's front oxygen sensor is indicating the engine is running lean (too much air). Common causes are a small air leak or a sensor that's aging.

P1135.name: Air/Fuel Ratio Sensor Heater Circuit Response (Toyota/Lexus)
symptoms: poor fuel economy on cold start
tests: check A/F sensor heater circuit resistance
P1135.advisor_summary: Your Toyota's air-fuel ratio sensor heater has a fault. These sensors help the engine run efficiently — a failed heater affects cold-start performance and fuel economy.

P1345.name: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation (GM)
tests: check timing chain stretch with scan tool
P1345.advisor_summary: Your GM's engine timing is out of correlation between the crankshaft and camshaft. This is often an early indicator of timing chain wear, which we want to address before it fails.

P2004.name: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open
tests: command IMRC closed with scan tool and observe idle
inspect runner flaps for carbon buildup
P2004.advisor_summary: The intake manifold runner control flap is stuck open. These flaps optimize airflow at different RPMs — stuck open affects low-RPM performance. Sometimes carbon cleaning resolves it.

P2096.name: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean Bank 1
causes: exhaust leak near downstream O2 sensor
tests: inspect exhaust system for leaks near sensor
P2096.advisor_summary: The rear oxygen sensor is detecting a lean exhaust condition. This is often caused by a small exhaust leak near the sensor, which pulls in air and gives a false lean reading.

P2101.name: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
tests: monitor TPS1 and TPS2 correlation with scan tool
P2101.advisor_summary: Your electronic throttle control system has a performance fault. This may put your vehicle into reduced power mode as a safety measure. A thorough throttle body cleaning often resolves this.

P2111.name: Throttle Actuator Control System — Stuck Open
P2111.advisor_summary: Your electronic throttle plate may be stuck open. This is a safety issue that should be addressed promptly. We'll start with a thorough throttle body cleaning.

P2119.name: Throttle Actuator Control Throttle Body Range/Performance
tests: clean throttle body and relearn idle with scan tool
check for TSBs on throttle body
P2119.advisor_summary: Your throttle body isn't responding within its expected range. Cleaning the throttle body and performing an idle relearn procedure often resolves this.

P2135.name: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch A/B Voltage Correlation
causes: wiring fault between TPS A and B
dirty throttle body causing false reading
tests: monitor TPS A and TPS B values with scan tool (should be inverse)
P2135.advisor_summary: Your two throttle position sensors are giving conflicting readings. The car may go into reduced power mode as a safety measure. This is usually a sensor replacement or wiring repair.

P2195.name: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
tests: monitor O2 sensor switching with scan tool
P2195.advisor_summary: Your front oxygen sensor is stuck reading lean. O2 sensors typically last 100,000 miles — if yours is near that mileage, replacement is likely the solution.

P2197.name: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
P2197.advisor_summary: The oxygen sensor on the right bank of your engine is stuck reading lean. Likely an aging sensor that needs replacement.

P2270.name: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
causes: catalytic converter issue affecting sensor reading
tests: check downstream O2 sensor switching pattern
P2270.advisor_summary: Your downstream (after catalytic converter) oxygen sensor is giving a lean reading. This can sometimes accompany a catalyst efficiency code — we'll determine if the sensor or the converter is the root cause.

P2279.name: Intake Air System Leak
causes: loose clamp on air intake hose
tests: visual inspection of all intake hoses and clamps
P2279.advisor_summary: There's an air leak in your intake system — unmetered air is entering the engine, causing it to run lean. We'll use a smoke test to find the exact location quickly.

P2400.name: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.advisor_summary: Your evaporative emission leak detection pump has a circuit fault. This component checks for fuel vapor leaks automatically. No drivability impact, but needs repair for emissions compliance.

P2404.name: EVAP Emission System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit
tests: test EVAP pump output and sensor
P2404.advisor_summary: The sensor circuit in your EVAP leak detection pump has a fault. This is an emissions compliance issue with no impact on vehicle performance.

P2610.name: ECM/PCM Internal Engine Off Timer Performance
tests: check PCM power and ground connections
P2610.advisor_summary: Your engine computer has a minor internal timer fault. We'll check the battery and PCM connections first, and look for a software update before recommending a PCM replacement.

C0035.name: Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
tests: monitor wheel speed sensor readings with scan tool
C0035.advisor_summary: Your right front wheel speed sensor has a circuit fault. This disables your ABS and traction control systems — important safety features. We'll diagnose whether it's the sensor, wiring, or tone ring.

C0040.name: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
tests: compare all four WSS readings with scan tool
C0040.advisor_summary: Your right rear wheel speed sensor has a fault, disabling ABS and traction control. A relatively straightforward sensor or wiring repair.

C0045.name: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
C0045.advisor_summary: Your left rear wheel speed sensor has a circuit fault, disabling ABS. We'll test the sensor, wiring, and the tone ring that the sensor reads.

B1000.name: ECU Internal Malfunction (Airbag/SRS)
causes: power or ground issue to module
tests: pull SRS codes with airbag-capable scanner
check for prior impact events stored in module
B1000.advisor_summary: Your airbag system control module has flagged an internal fault. When the airbag light is on, the system may not deploy in an accident. This is a safety-critical repair that should be addressed promptly.

U0100.name: Lost Communication With ECM/PCM A
tests: check PCM power and ground fuses
scan all modules for network codes
U0100.advisor_summary: Your vehicle's computer network has lost communication with the main engine computer. This typically points to a power/ground issue with the PCM or a wiring fault on the communication bus. We'll trace the network to find the break.

U0101.name: Lost Communication With TCM
tests: check CAN bus between PCM and TCM
U0101.advisor_summary: The engine computer has lost contact with the transmission computer. This can trigger limp mode as a safety measure. We'll check the wiring between the two modules first.

U0155.name: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Control Module
tests: check instrument cluster fuse and power
verify CAN bus connection at cluster
U0155.advisor_summary: Your engine computer has lost contact with the instrument cluster. This can cause gauge failures and warning lights. We'll trace the communication wiring to find the fault.
